THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE K.SURENDER  CRIMINAL REVISION CASE No.1726 OF 2010 ORDER:
The revision petitioner was tried for the offence under Sections 376 and 307 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The case of PW.1-victim is that on the date of incident at about 2:30 p.m. when she was in her house, the accused went to her house, caught hold of her, dragged her into the room and thrown her on the ground.
He further caught hold of her breast and fisted on her lip.
The accused also gagged cloth in her mouth and committed rape on her after removing her clothes.
After completing the act of intercourse, the accused threatened the victim with an axe to kill her.
She shouted for help.
Her sister's son, Shankaraiah-PW.3 and PW.5-Krishnaiah along with PW.2- Kalamma and PW.4-Linga Swamy went there.
On seeking them, the accused fled.
Thereafter, PW.1 went to the Police Station and filed complaint which is Ex.P1.
PW.4-sister's son is not examined.
The Police during investigation sent PW.1 for the purpose of examination by the doctor-PW.9.

PW.9-doctor found four injuries on the victim-PW.1 which are;
i) Contusion on both lips measuring 3 X 3 ii) Contusion on both thighs measuring 3 X 3 iii) Fresh tear of vaginal orifices at 6'O clock position iv) Fracture of ribs of 7 to 9 on right side.
3. During the course of trial, PW.1 in her chief-examination narrated the incident and alleged that the accused committed rape on her and with M.O.1-Axe the accused threatened her.
It is further stated that her son and the accused are good friends.
During the course of cross-examination, she stated that she received injuries as she fell on the stones nearby.
The said version was given by her 20 days after the chief-examination and further cross examined on the recall application filed by the accused.
The trial Court convicted the accused both under Sections 376 and 307 of the Indian Penal Code.

In appeal, the learned Sessions Judge found that in view of the statement of the victim regarding the injuries, accused was acquitted under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code, however,
the conviction under Section 376 of IPC was maintained.
4. The learned Counsel appearing for the revision petitioner would submit that the victim herself had stated that she received injuries on account of fall on the stones.

She was aged 60 years, as such,
the question of committing rape on PW.1 does not arise.

The said version of PW.1 is not supported Sunkaraboina Sreeshailam, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., Trhgh ... on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115133599/

sentences.text: The doctor did not give positive opinion regarding rape being committed and only stated that rape could not be ruled out.
When the evidence of Doctor itself is doubtful and PW.1 has stated two different versions, one in chief-examination and other in cross- examination, her evidence cannot be believed.
Once her evidence is disbelieved, there is no other corroboration either from the Doctor or any other witnesses PWs.2 to 5.
For the said reason the conviction of the Courts below has to be reversed.
5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that the hostility of PW.1 was in the cross-examination which was permitted nearly 25 years after chief-examination.
The reason is that she was won over during the said time.
Since injuries were found on the victim and the doctor stated that rape cannot be ruled out, the finding by the Sessions Court has to be upheld.

6. PW.1 had initially stated that she was raped by the accused and thereafter when recalled for cross-examination, she resiled from her earlier version of committing rape and beating and stated that injuries that were received were on account of falling on the ground.
PW.1 herself admitted that what she stated in the chief- examination was incorrect.
PW.1 is a self-condemned witness.
In view of her dual version regarding the incident, the Court has to look into whether there is any corroborating evidence regarding the version given by PW.1.
According to PW.1, PWs.2 and 3 were eye-witnesses to the incident and PWs.4 and 5 arrived immediately after the incident.
On seeing PWs.2 to 5, the accused fled.
In fact, all the witnesses PWs.2 to 5 turned hostile to the prosecution case.
PW.4 is the son of victim-PW.1.
PW.1 herself stated that the cause of injuries was not the alleged assault or attack by PW.1.
The injuries, according to the prosecution case ware subsequent to the rape committed and in order to threaten PW.1 such injuries were caused.
The Sessions Court has disbelieved the version of beating PW.1.
The substratum of the prosecution case itself is disbelieved.
The case cannot be accepted in parts or partially, when the case itself is that rape was committed and subsequently beaten up, the Court cannot conclude that she was not beaten up.
But, as stated initially she was raped.
As already discussed, there is no corroboration either through the evidence of doctor, FSL report or the witnesses who are alleged eye-witnesses to the incident.
In the said circumstances, benefit of doubt is extended to the accused.

7. Accordingly, Criminal Revision Case stands allowed setting aside the Judgment dated 14.11.2009,
passed by the Judge, Family Court-cum-Additional District and Sessions Judge, Nalgonda, in Crl.A.No.120/2008 and the Revision petitioner is acquitted.
